q: I ate breakfast this morning and had to take a 3.5 almost 4 hour nap. I got up ate again and started getting laundry together. I felt like my legs were going to buckle out from under me
cx: At 33 weeks, exhaustion so heavy one load of laundry floors her.

q: My husband is working on cleaning the house, but he works a lot. I feel incredibly guilty. He and I are discussing getting a house cleaner to come in and help.
cx: Guilt that her husband cleans after long work days; a paid cleaner considered.

q: I'm just feeling guilty about it, plus there's a lot I want to do still to get prepped for our baby!
cx: Same author: tiredness collides with the preparation list.

q: I know my practice is willing to do VBAC, but I think because I’ve had two at this point, they’re going to push for another.
cx: Third pregnancy after two caesareans, weighing a trial of labour against the booked date.

q: this isn’t stressing me out - it’s really helpful to get an idea of what challenges people who were in a similar situation faced.
cx: UK woman told to deliver early, choosing between two routes; others' stories help rather than frighten.

q: It’s not the c-section that scares me, but rather the thought of being so exhausted after days of labor to just get the c-section.
cx: Facing a planned induction for a pregnancy condition; fears a long induction ending in surgery.

q: since so much of early pregnancy has been “just wait and see”, I feel like up until now I’ve just been coasting. Now I’m over 10 weeks and can take the NIPT and have my second appointment and an ultrasound scheduled for when I’m 11 weeks, but I feel so clueless on what to do or how to go about things.
cx: First-timer at 10 weeks: the waiting phase ends and she has no map.

q: so far everyone I’ve seen and talked to has told me mostly the same things but it doesn’t feel in depth enough? I’m still so confused?
cx: Care-team model, different clinician each visit; the information stays shallow.

q: I feel like I asked three people at my last appointment where the lab location is and no one told me exactly where.
cx: Told to walk in for a blood test; nobody says where, Google contradicts the clinic.

q: I feel ashamed and anxious that I was unable to figure it out myself lol. I feel like I should know what’s happening and what I’m doing but I have zero clue!!!
cx: Same author, after messaging her doctor with basic logistics questions.

q: if anyone has any advice or I guess book recommendations or other recommendations on how to try and figure out what the heck is going on that would be lovely 🥲 I’m spiraling
cx: Same author asks strangers for a book or anything that explains what happens next.

q: have already received comments from other, unrelated medical professionals telling me I can expect to be induced so that the doctors can be home for the holidays
cx: Due on New Year's; at 10 weeks she is already told to expect a holiday induction.

q: Because of the risk of some company’s firing pregnant people, I really really wanted to keep it a secret.
cx: About to start a job at her partner's company at 6 weeks; wanted no one at work told.

q: I get he was excited, but he didn’t really understand that I’m the one who absorbs the risk. Not him.
cx: Her partner told colleagues, and it reached her manager.

q: I said I felt like I was a surrogate for his experience instead of an active participant.
cx: Same author after he also shared the baby's sex before any family reveal.

q: Pregnancy is a shared experience with unequal participants and it’s truly so hard to navigate!
cx: Same author, reflecting on why his excitement overrode hers.

q: At least five people touched my 7 week old baby on the face/head at a family gathering.
cx: Felt pressured to bring her baby to a family event; hands on the baby before she could speak.

q: I’m also a registered nurse and my current position does not offer health insurance, I make too much to qualify for the state insurance and my first appointment is already going to cost $620.00.
cx: Second pregnancy ten years after the first; uninsured at 6 weeks.

q: it was a smooth 9 months. I had NO complaints at all and I was very grateful. 10 years later, I found at 2 weeks because I track my cycle now. I’m currently 6 weeks and miserable. I’ve been nauseous, exhausted and emotional since week 3.
cx: First pregnancy easy; the second is miserable from week 3.

q: I don’t have many friends or family support outside of my husband. Any tips or recommendations would be greatly appreciated!
cx: Same author; little support beyond her husband.

q: My doctor told me I need to “watch my diet and exercise more” which I literally don’t know how to do that unless I quit my job which isn’t an option.
cx: Baby measuring large on scans; the doctor's advice ignores her job and exhaustion.

q: To clarify - I barely have enough energy to work, much less exercise more.
cx: Same author, replying to commenters.

q: I’m terrified for the delivery and looking for some reassurance 😭
cx: Same author after a growth scan put her baby over the 99th percentile.
